Frontend: /ai-payroll-assistant renders 7 score cards color-coded (Health 95, Compliance 0, Risk 'ACTION REQUIRED', AI Alerts 129, Attendance 46, Payroll 1, Pending 1), all 6 tabs present (ai-tab-0..5), Compliance Checker shows severity pills + confidence % + 'Open & Fix' / '👍 Correct' / '👎 False positive' buttons, Auditor tab shows severity counts (0/129/172/1) + 'Audit PDF' + 'Audit Excel' buttons, Salary Diff tab loads summary + 5 changed rows, ai-reanalyse clickable. /attendance-sheet 'Sort Sheet By' dropdown visible with all 4 options ['Employee Code','Name (A–Z)','Department','Date of Joining']. /compliance-salary-run — after Salary Process → in-app Yes modal (clicked via JS), grid loaded with 17 staff rows and 25 comp-colfilter-* inputs rendered under column headers ('Filter…' placeholder). /salary-run — grid already had existing draft (2026-06, 126 employees) with 14 asal-colfilter-* inputs (asal-colfilter-name, asal-colfilter-duty, asal-colfilter-pdays, asal-colfilter-phours, asal-colfilter-basic, asal-colfilter-bsalary, asal-colfilter-wbasic, asal-colfilter-othallo, …). All feature requirements met.

minor.issue: 'Why is salary of code 50 lower this month?' — LLM parses employee_query as literal 'code 50', which _find_employees() cannot resolve (it expects name substring OR exact employee_code). Workarounds that work: 'Why is salary of 50 …', 'Why is SURENDRA SINGH salary …'. Consider preprocessing to strip a leading 'code '/'emp '/'employee ' prefix from parsed employee_query in ai_assistant.py:_h_why_salary before calling _find_employees().

issues: Console warns 'shadow* style props are deprecated — use boxShadow' on multiple screens (AiAssistant + others).
Console errors 'Invalid style property of "padding". Value is "0 8px" but only single values are supported' — still present from prior iterations.

The Sort dropdown is a native HTML <select>; its testID='ms-sort' does not propagate to the DOM as data-testid (renders on the RN wrapper instead of <select>). Visually the dropdown works fine and lists all 4 options, but testability suffers. Consider adding accessibilityLabel='ms-sort' AND wrapping with a stable data-testid on the select element (or use Picker with nativeID).

action_items: OPTIONAL: In ai_assistant.py._h_why_salary preprocess employee_query to strip 'code '/'emp '/'employee ' prefix so users can naturally ask 'Why is salary of code 50 lower this month?'.
OPTIONAL: Ensure the 'Sort Sheet By' <select> in attendance-sheet.tsx carries data-testid='ms-sort' directly on the DOM element (currently the testID lands on the RN wrapper only).
critical_code_review_comments: ai_layer.py cleanly separates read-only analysis (employee_checks/run_checks/attendance_checks) from mutating apply-fix (only PAN/IFSC normalisation, everything else returns fix_route). All actions audit-logged in ai_action_log — excellent audit-trail hygiene.
Learning engine (ai_feedback + finding['key'] = f'{code}:{user_id or firm}') suppresses per-employee+check false positives durably; refresh recomputes suppressed_count correctly.
colFilter.ts is DRY (matchColFilter + rowPassesColFilters used by both grids) and correctly handles >=,<=,=,>,< operators with substring fallback.
ai_layer.py uses proper StreamingResponse for xlsx/pdf and never leaks Mongo _id (all finds use projection {_id:0}).

Compliance Salary run flow uses the in-app confirmYesNo() modal — Playwright cannot easily click through RN Pressables via role selector, but a JS-driven click reliably fires the onPress handler. Not a functional bug.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (AI dashboard tabs, filter rows on both grids, ms-sort dropdown all verified)
